newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday due to a strong rebound on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
But the annual rate for the most active three-day contract fell to 3.6 percent from 12.2 percent on Thursday because of the weekend factor.
The fact that borrowers of the contract can only use the funds for one day with the markets closing for two days at each weekend generally depresses the contract's rates on Fridays.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 6.32 million lots from 12.05 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the rebound on the A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen on Friday after Thursday's plunge had made institutions borrow on the repo market, supporting the rates.
There is no new A share issue on the two exchanges on Friday, limiting the fund demand on the repo market and reducing the volume, they said.
Traders said the performance of the A share markets would continue to be a key factor for the repo rate movements early next week with no other market-moving news in sight.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday.

The 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, rose to 116.40 yuan from 116.22, indicating the market would begin to roll back from a powerful two-week technical correction starting early last week, traders said.
The most active three-year bond maturing in August 1999 fell slightly to 105.17 yuan from 105.20 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.22 million lots from 1.13 million lots.
